title: Redwood discovery - AstraPay latency & throughput
meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-04 | Time: 15:00 PT | Duration: 52m | Recording: https://redwood.zoom/rec/mtg-20260304-astrapay | Attendees: Maya T, Samir P (Redwood); Lena O, Daniel K, Priya S (AstraPay)
summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency targets, expected concurrency, streaming vs non-streaming use, and token/sec benchmarking. AstraPay is leaning toward Redwood Dedicated for predictable p95 but is evaluating hosted with fallbacks and Private for compliance. Action items: share benchmark template & pricing, customer to provide sample payloads and target SLOs.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood. We'll run through a quick discovery on latency and throughput goals, then Samir will do a quick technical Q. Uh if anyone can't hear just shout.
[00:18] Lena (CTO): Hi all, thanks. I'm Lena, CTO at AstraPay. We're mostly concerned with p95 under load for our fraud-check model, and also streaming for customer-facing chats.
[00:28] Samir (SE): great, quick context question, is the fraud model synchronous in the request path or async? like is 200ms vs 500ms materially different for you?
[00:38] Daniel (ML Engineer): It's sync. For token classification we need sub-300ms p95 for single-turn rejects, but for multi-turn chat customer support we can tolerate up to 800ms p95.
[00:52] Priya (SRE): Our peak concurrent users hit about 1800 concurrent inference calls across region during promos; baseline is 300. We're trying to understand how Redwood can hit p95 at 1800 concurrency with streaming enabled.
[01:10] Maya (AE): helpful. Two quick axes: model size/architecture and whether you're streaming incremental tokens. Samir, should I jump in?
[01:18] Samir (SE): yeah I'll ask the infra stuff. What model family and sequence lengths are we looking at? Also any current token/sec numbers from your infra?
[01:28] Daniel: We're running a finetuned Llama-2-7b variant for fraud and a 13b for chat. Typical prompt+response avg 120 tokens, peak up to 400 for chat transcripts. Right now our on-prem tests show ~250 tokens/sec on p95 per GPU for the 13b but that's with older quant.
[01:45] Samir: ok so rough order, 13b at 250 tps per GPU means scaling math for 1800 conc depends on concurrency model — continuous batching can push tokens/sec higher but increases tail. For p95 we usually recommend Dedicated or Private to control SLOs.
[02:02] Lena: can you clarify that? Why not Hosted for us? We like not managing infra.
[02:08] Maya: good question. Hosted is great for time-to-value; we publish performance profiles. But Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput with SLA-backed p95 targets; Private gives you VPC/on-prem control for compliance. For strict p95 at high concurrency we often see customers pick Dedicated.
[02:26] Daniel: streaming — does Redwood support partial token streaming for early responses? We need first-token latency under 150ms for chat.
[02:35] Samir: yes, streaming with chunked flush is supported. First-token latency is mostly network + model step time, so with an optimized kernel on A100/A800-ish hardware we can get first-token p95 into the 100-150ms ballpark for smaller prompts. But with longer prefixes or KV cache misses that will increase. Also "KV cash" — sorry, I mean KV cache behavior matters for chat.
[02:58] Priya: network wise we will be in GCP us-central and also have EU region. We require VPC peering and SAML SSO and KMS integration. Can Redwood-hosted do customer-managed KMS?
[03:10] Maya: Hosted supports customer-managed keys for enterprise tier via KMS integration and private endpoints for traffic. For strict network isolation Private is the option.
[03:18] Lena: curious about benchmarks — you'd run a tokens/sec benchmark DSL? What artifacts do you need?
[03:25] Samir: we have a benchmark template (spreadsheet + harness) we share. We'll need sample prompts, sample concurrency profile (ramp, steady state), token distributions, and expected p95 targets.
[03:36] Daniel: I can export traces from our load tests; we have token length histograms and 95/99 latencies.
[03:42] Samir: perfect. For a POC we propose two phases: 1) Hosted quick benchmark against published model profile (3-5k requests) to validate latency targets, 2) Dedicated pilot with reserved pool to validate p95 at scale and run streaming tests. If compliance requires, Private pilot for VPC and KMS validation.
[03:58] Maya: cost tradeoffs matter too. Dedicated is more predictable but with commit; hosted is variable cost. We can run cost per 1M tokens estimates in the pricing deck.
[04:09] Lena: our p95 SLOs: fraud model <300ms p95, chat first-token <150ms p95, full chat response <800ms p95. Concurrency target 1800 sustained at peak.
[04:22] Priya: also need audit logs and retention 12 months, SOC2 compliance, and RBAC review.
[04:29] Maya: we have SOC 2 + ISO docs, audit-log export, and RBAC. We'll attach security docs.
[04:35] Daniel: sample workload question, do you recommend continuous batching or single-request low-latency mode? We've seen batching reduce cost but raise tail latencies.
[04:44] Samir: right — batching reduces tokens/sec cost. Our runtime supports adaptive batching and KV-aware batching. For strict p95 you can bias toward smaller batch sizes with CPU/GPU pre-warm to keep tail low; Dedicated allows you to set policies.
[04:59] Lena: how do fallbacks work if Dedicated pool is saturated during flash sales?
[05:04] Samir: we offer smart routing — route-by-policy to fall back to hosted or lower-cost variants and automatic graceful degradation. You can set model variant fallbacks and region fallback. There's a slight latency/cost tradeoff but keeps availability.
[05:18] Priya: will the fallback preserve data residency? That's important for EU data.
[05:22] Maya: fallbacks can be region-aware; you can restrict fallback policies so EU stays in EU.
[05:28] Daniel: any noise/imperfection notes — our internal benchmark had noise around tokenization diff causing +10% token counts, sometimes the transcriptions mix up LLM names, have you seen that?
[05:37] Samir: totally, tokenization differences between tokenizers matter. We'll align tokenization settings as part of the benchmark.
[05:43] Lena: timeline — we want to start a POC in two weeks and aim for production by end of Q2 if numbers look good.
[05:50] Maya: sounds realistic. Next steps recap at end and we'll capture action items.
[06:00] Maya: quick note— do you have any specific throughput target in tokens/sec overall we should try to hit?
[06:05] Daniel: at peak, with 1800 concurrency and average 120 tokens per request that’s ~216k tokens/sec ingest; we expect batching to reduce GPU count but need p95 guarantees.
[06:18] Samir: that's helpful math. 216k tokens/sec aggregate means we'll propose a Dedicated config and map to GPUs based on your model 13b profile — expect to nominate n1 A100-equivalent GPUs. We'll provide exact counts in the benchmark plan.
[06:33] Priya: any limitations with streaming and large concurrency re: connection limits?
[06:38] Samir: we recommend HTTP/2 or websocket streaming. Connection scaling handled at the edge; we can put nginx or LB in front. We'll share recommendations for socket pools.
[06:48] Lena: ok, security quick: we need SAML metadata and a SOC2 attestation — please attach.
[06:53] Maya: will do.
[06:55] (crosstalk) Daniel: one more, are there per-token preprocessing costs like detokenization in your pipeline?
[07:02] Samir: minimal in runtime, most token work is in the model forward. If you have heavy pre/post processing we recommend offloading to preproc pods to keep GPU focused.
[07:12] Maya: alright let's capture next steps and owners.
[07:16] Lena: that works.
[07:18] Maya: recap — we will send: pricing deck, benchmark template + harness link, SOC2/KMS/RBAC docs, and a proposed Dedicated pilot config. AstraPay will provide: sample prompt set, token-length histograms, current load traces, and target SLOs. We'll schedule a technical deep-dive for the Dedicated pilot.
[07:36] Priya: thanks everyone.
[07:38] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up via CRM and email. Bye.
